english.title: Channel tunnel - place a device in the tunnel
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) unlawfully and intentionally placed in the Channel Tunnel system

(A)_[a device,]_
(B)_[devices,]_
(C)_[a substance,]_
(D)_[substances,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY..), which

(E)_[was]_
(F)_[were]_

likely

(G)_[to destroy the tunnel system]_
(H)_[so to damage the tunnel system as to endanger its safety]_
english.legislation: Contrary to article 6(2)(b) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
unlawfully intentionally placed in the channel tunnel system
device(s) / substance(s) likely to destroy the tunnel system
likely so to damage the tunnel system as to endanger its safety

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Attorney General is required, see article 9(1) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994.
(ii) See also offence wording at: H1377.
(iii) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property.

other.penalty:
Life imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
